title: Close out a shadow board and flag the missing tool
instruction: Put each tool on its matching outline, the stray part that matches no outline in the yellow FOD bin, and the red tag on the outline whose tool is missing. A brass chit means that tool is signed out.
context: Tool control is part of foreign object debris (FOD) prevention on spacecraft and aircraft integration floors. Tools live on shadow boards; a signed-out tool leaves a chit on its outline, and at closeout every outline must hold its tool or a chit. A bare outline without a chit means a tool may be inside the vehicle, so work stops and that outline is flagged. Loose hardware that belongs to no board is debris and goes in the FOD bin. The test is reasoning about an absence: match three tools to their outlines by shape and size, see that one loose part matches no outline, and flag the bare outline. The two empty outlines are the same shape and size, so only the chit tells them apart. The excused one is nearest the tag and ends the row; the bare one is off the board centre, so no habit of fit, size, proximity or centre finds it. The flag carries 0.40 because it is the call a technician makes at closeout; each placement carries 0.15. A 1 g bench analogue of work done in 1 g.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = +0.305. All parts are rigid matte primitives with one friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed: the shadow board, a white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90) block 100 (x) x 280 (y) x 30 mm standing on the table centred at (0.280, 0.305), spanning x 0.230 to 0.330 and y 0.165 to 0.445. On its top, five solid dark grey (sRGB 0.20, 0.20, 0.22) silhouettes, filled shapes cut from 1 mm card and called outlines below, all centred on x = 0.280: wrench, a 76 x 26 mm rectangle long along x, at y = 0.410; socket, a 42 mm disc, at y = 0.355; adapter, a 46 x 46 mm square, at y = 0.300; pliers, a 66 x 36 mm rectangle long along x, at y = 0.240; side cutters, the same 66 x 36 mm rectangle, at y = 0.190. A brass (sRGB 0.78, 0.62, 0.25) chit, 30 (x) x 24 x 3 mm, fixed flat on the cutters outline at its centre (0.280, 0.190). The FOD bin: four yellow (sRGB 0.90, 0.80, 0.10) walls 6 mm thick and 35 mm tall standing on the table round an open pocket 130 (x) x 100 (y) mm centred at (0.140, 0.545), so the pocket spans x 0.075 to 0.205 and y 0.495 to 0.595 and the outer outline is 142 x 112 mm; the table is its floor. Loose, standing on the table in a row at x = 0.150, stand-in props: the wrench, a steel grey (sRGB 0.55, 0.56, 0.58) box 20 (x) x 70 (y) x 20 mm, 45 g, at y = 0.405, a quarter turn from its outline; the socket, a dark steel (sRGB 0.35, 0.35, 0.37) upright cylinder 36 mm across and 30 mm tall, 50 g, at y = 0.330; the stray bracket (the debris), a steel grey box 18 (x) x 36 (y) x 30 mm, 25 g, at y = 0.265; the adapter, a blue (sRGB 0.20, 0.35, 0.70) box 40 x 40 x 25 mm, 55 g, turned 30 degrees, at y = 0.195; the red (sRGB 0.85, 0.10, 0.10) tag, a box 24 (x) x 50 (y) x 20 mm, 12 g, at y = 0.120. Each outline is 3 mm per side larger than its tool. The bracket matches no outline, no loose part matches the pliers or cutters outline, and those two are identical, so only the chit tells them apart. The board is as tall as the tallest loose part and the bin walls are taller than the bracket. Nothing touches at the start. To build it: a 30 mm board or foam block painted white, the outlines as filled silhouettes cut from 1 mm dark card and glued on, and a brass-coloured card chit glued on the cutters outline; the bin from 6 x 35 mm strip glued round the pocket; the props cut from wood and weighted to the stated masses; tape the board and the bin to the table.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo, a tape measure and a phone level. A tool is home when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s) and square on the board (lowest point within 4 mm of the board top, so on the board or an outline and not on another part; a face within 5 degrees of level) with its centre within 8 mm of its own outline's centre, and turned to match: the wrench on either 20 mm face with its long axis within 10 degrees of its outline's, either way round; the adapter on a 40 x 40 face, either way up, with its edges within 10 degrees of its outline's, any quarter turn; the socket standing on either end, any yaw. The bracket is binned when it is at rest with its centre inside the bin's inner walls seen from above and its lowest point no more than 10 mm above the table (standing, lying or leaning on the bin floor), and no tool and not the tag is in the bin (centre inside the inner walls, lowest point under the wall tops). The tag counts when it is at rest and square on the board (lowest point within 4 mm of the board top, any face down within 5 degrees of level) with its centre within 15 mm of the pliers outline's centre. Score = 0.15 for each of the three tools home, plus 0.15 for the bracket binned, plus 0.40 for the tag on the pliers outline: 0, 0.15, 0.30, 0.40, 0.45, 0.55, 0.60, 0.70, 0.85 or 1.0. Override: the bracket anywhere on the board (centre over the board's footprint, lowest point no lower than 4 mm under the board top) makes the score 0 whatever else is right. The board is the tool count: a part that is not its tool sitting on it can make a bare outline read as filled and hide the missing tool, so it voids the closeout, while the bracket left on the table is only unbinned. A tag on the cutters outline or its chit (a false alarm on a signed-out tool), on any other outline, on a tool, held or moving earns no tag credit. A tool on another tool's outline earns nothing. Dumping every loose part in the bin scores 0. The start state scores 0. Pushing cannot score: the board is 30 mm tall, as tall as the tallest loose part, so nothing reaches its top without being lifted, and the 35 mm bin walls stand taller than the 30 mm bracket. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. In simulation every test uses each part's centre and quaternion; the lowest point comes from the part's own extents and rotation, not the axis-aligned bounds. The board, outlines, chit and bin are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which any of them moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. In simulation release is inferred from a part being at rest, so a part held motionless in a scoring place would count; on real arms the photo is taken after the gripper opens and moves clear.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the five loose parts back on their marks in the row, the wrench's long axis along y and the adapter turned 30 degrees; the board, outlines, chit and bin do not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the open-loop demo is planned from the nominal marks, and with jitter each part would start up to 3 cm off its mark.
fidelity: Approximate: two boxes and a cylinder stand in for a wrench, a socket and an adapter, and a box for a loose bracket; the pliers and cutters are absent by design. Matching rests on outline size and shape alone, and the outlines are solid 1 mm card silhouettes rather than painted ones. The board lies flat on the bench, not on a wall. Rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench, which is where closeout is done.
